clientName.description: The computer's name on the network.

path2.description: The new name, for a rename.

count.description: How many times it happened while active.

details.description: Machine-readable facts for the UI (affected files, counts...).

key.description: Which one (a share, an IP...); "" when there is only one.

kind.description: What happened, e.g. "samba.reload_failed". Stable: the UI may switch on it.

message.description: What happened and what to do, for a person.

address.description: An IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64 range.

mac.description: The device's hardware address, when it is on the local network.

offence.description: 1 for a first ban; higher for repeats within a week (longer bans).

reason.description: "same_device": a banned device came back with a new address.

allowList.description: Addresses and ranges never banned (your own computer). IPs or CIDR ranges.

banMinutes.description: How long the first ban lasts. Each repeat within a week lasts 4 times longer.

enabled.description: Count failed SMB logins and ban addresses that fail too often. Also turns on login logging in Samba.

followDevice.description: When a banned computer on the local network gets a new address (DHCP), ban the new address too (recognised by its hardware/MAC address).

windowMinutes.description: ... within this many minutes, to be banned.

chap.description: The client must also give the CHAP secret (iSCSI). The secret is never shown again.

client.description: The one computer that may connect: its iSCSI initiator name (iqn...) or NVMe host name (nqn...).

connected.description: The client is connected now (iSCSI only).

device.description: A whole disk given to the client, by its /dev/disk/by-id link.

imageFolder.description: Image-backed: the folder of the image file (<folder>/d<id>.img).

target.description: The iSCSI target name or NVMe subsystem name to connect to.

confirmDevice.description: When giving a whole disk: its path again.

confirmSingleClient.description: Must be true: only ONE computer may ever use this disk; two at once destroy its contents.

device.description: Or give a whole disk (see GET /block/devices). Its contents become the client's.

imageFolder.description: Make an image file in this folder (not a share).

listen.description: The address to listen on (default 0.0.0.0: every address).

protocol.description: iSCSI works on Windows, macOS (with an initiator) and Linux, and can require a CHAP secret. NVMe/TCP is faster, but Windows has no built-in client, and it checks only the host name, which a client can copy: use it on a network you trust.

chapUser.description: Empty (with an empty secret) turns CHAP off.

sizeGiB.description: Grow only: shrinking would cut off the client's data.

access.description: Users who may use the share. Without any (and without guest access), nobody can connect.

createDirectory.description: Create the folder if it does not exist. Its parent must exist.

guestAccess.description: Anyone on the network can read without a password.

hideUnreadable.description: Hide files and folders a user cannot read. Slows down listing very big folders.

path.description: Full path of the folder on the server.

preset.description: The preset used to set the share up (a label; see GET /shares/presets). Default "custom".

readOnly.description: Nobody can change files, whatever their level.

timeMachine.description: Macs can back up into this share (see Share.timeMachine). Turns Mac support on.

timeMachineMaxGiB.description: The size Time Machine sees as the disk, in GiB (0: the real disk's size).

smbAccess.description: Give the user a Samba account so they can be added to shares. Defaults to true.

hint.description: What to do when the service cannot be switched on.

installed.description: A package provides the daemon (wsdd or wsdd2; avahi-daemon).

on.description: Running and enabled: what the toggle shows.

mdns.description: mDNS / Bonjour: the server shows up in macOS Finder and Linux file managers, and Macs find Time Machine shares.

systemd.description: False when the machine is not run by systemd: the daemons cannot be switched from here.

wsd.description: WS-Discovery: the server shows up in Windows' Network folder, under the machine's hostname.

path.description: Target folder to benchmark (defaults to the server data directory).

sizeMiB.description: Test file size in MiB (1–128, default 32).

reason.description: Why, in words for the user.

note.description: One sentence about everyone not listed.

passphrase.description: Encrypts the file. Needed to restore it: it cannot be recovered.

smbPasswords.description: Include the Samba password hashes, so users keep their SMB passwords after a restore (default true). Without them, SMB users must be given new passwords.

field.description: Name of the invalid field, e.g. "username".

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show next to the field.

blocked.description: The user was made read-only (until restored).

path.description: Inside the share, with / between folders. "" is the share's top folder.

attempts.description: How many times the job was started; more than 1 means it was resumed after a restart.

title.description: Shown to the user, e.g. "Copy 3 items to Media".

total.description: Units of work in total; 0 while unknown.

total.description: Total number of matching items across all pages.

path.description: The new folder, inside the share. Its parent must exist.

level.description: What the user can effectively do.

asUserId.description: Mode "user": the user the clients act as. Must have read or write on the share.

clients.description: The computers that may mount the share. Required: an NFS export is never open to every address.

enabled.description: Export the share over NFS to the listed clients.

mode.description: "user": the clients act as one user (asUserId) and get that user's access. "client-ids": the clients' own user ids are trusted (only for trusted Linux machines with the same accounts); root is always mapped to nobody.

address.description: An IP address (192.168.1.50) or a range in CIDR form (192.168.1.0/24). IPv4 or IPv6.

readOnly.description: This client can only read, whatever the share allows.

exports.description: The shares exported over NFS right now.

hint.description: What to do when NFS cannot be used yet.

running.description: The kernel NFS server is running.

supported.description: False where an NFS server cannot run at all (an unprivileged container).

address.description: An IP address (192.168.1.50) or a range in CIDR form (192.168.1.0/24). IPv4 or IPv6.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show to the user.

requestId.description: Quote this ID to find the matching server logs.

title.description: Short summary of the HTTP status.

type.description: Always "about:blank"; use "code" to identify the error.

name.description: The new name (no folders: use move for that).

bandwidthKiB.description: Bandwidth limit in KiB/s (0: no limit).

enabled.description: Scheduled runs happen. Manual runs work either way.

excludes.description: rsync patterns of files to leave out (like *.tmp or cache/).

localPath.description: A folder on this machine (a second disk). It may not be or hold a share.

mirror.description: Delete files at the destination that are gone from the share. Off: deleted files are kept there.

localPath.description: A folder on this machine (a second disk).

mirror.description: Delete files at the destination that are gone from the share.

mac.description: HMAC-SHA256 over the request, keyed with the code's secret.

receiver.description: The receiving folder, from the pairing code.

mac.description: HMAC-SHA256 over the whole exchange, keyed with the code's secret.

hostKey.description: The peer's SSH host key, pinned when it was paired.

code.description: The pairing code made on the other NetShare Hub (Replication, Receiving folders).

url.description: The other NetShare Hub's web address, like http://192.168.1.20:8080.

code.description: Enter it on the sending NetShare Hub within 15 minutes. It works once.

path.description: A new folder for the copies, like /srv/replicas/office. It may not be or hold a share.

changes.description: A preview's list of changes (at most 1000), as rsync itemizes them.

files.description: Files and folders at the source.

taskId.description: The background job that runs it (see /jobs).

transferred.description: Files copied (or, in a preview, that would be).

rrsync.description: Needed to receive copies (comes with rsync 3.2.4 or newer).

sshClient.description: Needed to copy to a peer.

createMissingFolders.description: Create share folders that do not exist on this machine (their parent folder must exist).

dryRun.description: Only check the backup and say what restoring it would do. Nothing is changed.

job.description: Set when the rest runs as a background job; follow it in the jobs list.

activityLog.description: Record who did what over SMB (the activity log). Needs Samba's full_audit module (Debian, Ubuntu: samba-vfs-modules).

encryption.description: "if-supported" encrypts when the client can; "required" refuses clients that cannot (needs minProtocol SMB3_00 or newer).

macSupport.description: Apple's SMB extensions on every share: faster folders and correct file details on Macs. Needs Samba's fruit, catia and streams_xattr modules (Debian, Ubuntu: samba-vfs-modules). On while any share is a Time Machine share.

maxProtocol.description: The newest SMB version clients may use.

minProtocol.description: The oldest SMB version clients may use. SMB1 is never allowed.

multichannel.description: Several network links per client, for speed.

serverName.description: The server's name on the network (\\NAME): 1-15 letters, digits or -. Empty: keep the system's.

workgroup.description: The Windows workgroup: 1-15 letters, digits or -. Empty: keep the system's (usually WORKGROUP).

machine.description: The client's name or address as Samba knows it.

csrfToken.description: Send this back in the X-CSRF-Token header on every POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE.

permissions.description: Everything this user may do. Use it to show or hide UI; the server still checks every request.

mode.description: "learning" only raises alerts (start here); "protect" also makes the user read-only on every share and disconnects their computer.

noteFolders.description: In how many folders a ransom note (HOW_TO_DECRYPT...) must appear within a minute.

renames.description: Suspicious renames (to an unusual or known-bad extension) by one user from one computer within a minute that trigger the guard.

needsSetup.description: True until the first admin account has been created.

access.description: Users given access. Nobody else can connect, unless guest access is on.

guestAccess.description: Anyone on the network can read without a password, and every user with SMB access can read with theirs.

hideUnreadable.description: Hide files and folders a user cannot read, over SMB and in the file manager. Slows down listing very big folders.

networkRules.description: Which computers may connect. With any "allow" rule, only those addresses may; "block" rules never may. Empty: any address.

nfs.description: Export over NFS, to the listed computers only.

path.description: The folder on the server, with symbolic links resolved.

preset.description: The preset the share was set up with, or "custom". A label only: the rules are the other fields.

readOnly.description: Nobody can change files, whatever their level.

timeMachine.description: Macs can back up into this share with Time Machine. Its users need "write"; never a guest or read-only share.

timeMachineMaxGiB.description: The size Time Machine sees as the disk, in GiB (0: the real disk's size).

level.description: "read" = read only, "upload" = add files without seeing the folder (drop box), "write" = read and write.
"read" = read only, "upload" = add files without seeing the folder (drop box), "write" = read and write.

dailyTime.description: Local wall-clock time HH:MM for daily or weekly mode.

schedule.description: Human-readable schedule, e.g. "every 1h0m0s", "daily at 03:00", or "weekly on Sun at 02:30".

weekday.description: Day of week (0=Sun..6=Sat) for weekly mode.

app.description: The NetShare Hub version that made it.

applied.description: False for a dry run: nothing was changed.

hostname.description: The machine it was made on.

missingFolders.description: Share folders not on this machine (created when createMissingFolders is set).

rollbackCopy.description: The copy of the database kept before restoring (in the data folder's backups).

signInAgain.description: Everyone was signed out, the caller too: sign in with an account from the backup.

smbUsers.description: Users with SMB access after the restore.

conflict.description: When a file with the same name is there already: "rename" keeps both (default), "replace" overwrites it, "skip" leaves it.

destination.description: The folder to put them in.

dailyTime.description: Local time HH:MM (00:00–23:59) when mode is "daily" or "weekly".

enabled.description: Turn this background task on or off. Disabled tasks never run automatically.

everyMinutes.description: Interval in minutes (1–10080) when mode is "interval".

weekday.description: Day of week (0=Sunday..6=Saturday) when mode is "weekly".

networkRules.description: Replaces the whole list of network rules.

timeMachine.description: Turning it on turns Mac support on.

smbAccess.description: Turning this on needs "password" in the same request. Turning it off removes the user from every share.
True when the user has a Linux + Samba account and can be given access to shares. False means web login only.

url.description: Open it (GET) to download the zip. Works once, for a minute.
